record.paper_title: The Volume of Vector Fields on Riemannian Manifolds: Main Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Hopf-field uniqueness for minimal vector fields
record.original_question: Let S^{2m+1} be the unit odd-dimensional sphere in R^{2m+2}, let N be its outward unit normal field, and call a vector field of the form r JN a Hopf vector field, where J is a complex structure on R^{2m+2} and r > 0 is constant. Is every smooth minimal vector field of constant length on S^{2m+1} a Hopf vector field?

evidence.quote: the vector field of the form J N is known as a Hopf field
Conjecture 3.1 The only minimal smooth vector fields of constant length on the odd-dimensional spheres are the Hopf vector fields.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^{2m+1}\subset \mathbb{R}^{2m+2}$ denote the unit sphere of odd dimension $2m+1$, equipped with the round metric induced from the Euclidean metric on $\mathbb{R}^{2m+2}$. Let $N$ be the outward unit normal vector field of $S^{2m+1}$ in $\mathbb{R}^{2m+2}$. For any orthogonal complex structure $J$ on $\mathbb{R}^{2m+2}$ (i.e., a linear isometry with $J^2=-\mathrm{Id}$) and any constant $r>0$, the tangent vector field $V = r\,JN$ on $S^{2m+1}$ is called a Hopf vector field (of length $r$).

A smooth tangent vector field $V$ on $S^{2m+1}$ is said to have constant length if $\|V_p\|$ is independent of $p\in S^{2m+1}$, and is called minimal if its image $V(S^{2m+1})\subset TS^{2m+1}$, viewed as a submanifold of the tangent bundle equipped with the Sasaki metric, is a minimal submanifold (equivalently, $V$ is a critical point of the volume functional $\mathrm{vol}(V)=\int_{S^{2m+1}} \sqrt{\det(\mathrm{Id}+(\nabla V)^t \nabla V)}\,d\mathrm{vol}$ among vector fields of the same constant length).

Question: Is every smooth minimal vector field of constant length on $S^{2m+1}$ a Hopf vector field?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is generally regarded as an open conjecture. Hopf vector fields are known to be minimal on every odd-dimensional sphere, and partial evidence (volume minimization on $S^3$ by Gluck–Ziller, stability for small radii on $S^{2m+1}$, and uniqueness results on punctured spheres) supports the conjecture, but no full classification of smooth minimal constant-length vector fields on $S^{2m+1}$ has been established.

status_evidence.title: Minimal Vector Fields of Constant Length on the Odd-Dimensional Spheres
status_evidence.snippet: Hopf vector fields are the only known examples of smooth minimal vector fields of constant length on the whole odd sphere.
status_evidence.claim: The classification of minimal constant-length vector fields on odd-dimensional spheres remains an open conjecture, with Hopf fields as the only known examples.

status_evidence.title: A critical radius for unit Hopf vector fields on spheres
status_evidence.snippet: There is a critical radius below which Hopf fields are stable; this supports the Gluck–Ziller-type conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results support the conjecture but do not resolve uniqueness.

status_evidence.title: Vector Fields of Constant Length on Punctured Spheres
status_evidence.snippet: Studies minimal constant-length vector fields on spheres with points removed.
status_evidence.claim: Related partial uniqueness results have been obtained on punctured spheres.
